stories.headline: US approves $24.3B sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia as the Iran war drags on

key_facts.fact: The US State Department said on Thursday, September 17, that it approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth fighters to Saudi Arabia, the kingdom's largest arms purchase since the Iran war began.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States has approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes to Saudi Arabia, the State Department said Thursday, the kingdom's latest major arms purchase since the start of the Iran war.

key_facts.fact: The State Department notified Congress of the proposed sale, which still requires lawmakers' approval, and gave no delivery timetable.
key_facts.excerpt: The State Department has notified Congress about the proposed sale, which would require the approval of US lawmakers. It did not provide a time frame for the delivery of the jets.

key_facts.fact: Israel, currently the only Middle East country operating the F-35, has voiced concern about selling the jet to Riyadh despite the push for normalisation.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia has long sought to buy F-35s, but officials from Israel – currently the only country in the Middle East to operate the jets – have voiced concern about their sale to Riyadh despite a push for the kingdom to normalise relations.

key_facts.fact: The jet deal follows a $5 billion sale of more than 10,000 bombs approved earlier in September, a $750 million sale of 60 tank engines this month and a $1.96 billion July deal for precision guidance kits.
key_facts.excerpt: The State Department announced the approval of a $5 billion sale of more than 10,000 bombs – including highly destructive 2,000-pound weapons – to Riyadh earlier in September. Washington also signed off on the sale of 60 tank engines and related equipment to Saudi Arabia at a cost of $750 million this month, and a $1.96 billion deal in July

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia is simultaneously trading strikes with Yemen's Houthis: Saudi warplanes hit Hajjah and Taiz on Thursday and Riyadh said drone debris from an intercepted Houthi attack killed one person.
key_facts.excerpt: Houthi-controlled television reported fresh Saudi air strikes on Thursday in Hajjah province close to the Saudi border near the Red Sea coast, and the vicinity of Taiz further inland to the south.

sources.title: US approves $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 warplanes to Saudi Arabia
Saudis and Houthis exchange strikes, Yemenis take to boats to flee as Middle East war spreads

stories.headline: US diesel hits an all-time record near $6.40 a gallon as Iran keeps Hormuz shut

key_facts.fact: The average US retail diesel price set an all-time record on Thursday, September 17, just shy of $6.40 a gallon, while crude eased slightly but stayed above $100 a barrel.
key_facts.excerpt: Global crude prices eased slightly on Thursday but remain well above $100 a barrel after shooting to the highest levels since May. The cost of fuel for consumers has risen even more sharply, with the average retail price for diesel in the United States setting a new all-time record on Thursday just shy of $6.40 a gallon.

key_facts.fact: A political adviser to Iran's supreme leader, Mohammad-Bagher Zolghadr, said on September 17 that Iran will keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until Trump and Netanyahu are out of power.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our fighters will not open the Strait of Hormuz until the criminal Trump and bloodthirsty Netanyahu are brought down from power," Mohammad-Bagher Zolghadr said, describing the closure as the first stage of Iran's retaliation.

key_facts.fact: Only three commodity vessels transited Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 12 the previous day and far below the 10-day average of about 17, according to ship-tracking data.
key_facts.excerpt: Only three commodity vessels transited the waterway on Wednesday, down from 12 a day earlier and far below the 10-day average of about 17, Reuters reported, citing preliminary ship-tracking data.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, the main alternative route for Gulf crude, has been shut since it was struck last week in an attack Riyadh blamed on Iraq-based militias.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, which allowed it to pump oil across the Arabian Peninsula and ship it from the Red Sea, has been shut since it was struck last week in an attack Riyadh said came from Iraq, where Iran-backed militias also operate.

key_facts.fact: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians filled downtown Tehran on September 18 in the biggest state-orchestrated show of defiance since the war began, as the Revolutionary Guard said it struck another tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Hundreds of thousands of Iranians filled downtown Tehran in a government-orchestrated show of defiance, vowing to take up arms as war with the United States and Israel grinds on... the Guard says it struck another tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, further choking global energy flows.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on September 16-17 that he hoped the war was nearing its end and that "Iran is very much wanting to make a deal"; he is expected to meet Gulf leaders at the UN General Assembly next Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: "Well, hopefully we're toward the end of the war," Trump told reporters. "Iran is very much wanting to make a deal. We'll see how that works out." ... Trump is also expected to meet leaders or foreign ministers from the six Persian Gulf states on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next Tuesday

stories.headline: Russia's first wartime Duma election opens as 350 Ukrainian drones hit Moscow

key_facts.fact: Voting began on Friday, September 18, in a three-day Russian parliamentary election for the 450-seat State Duma, the first since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Voting got underway on Friday in a three-day parliamentary election in Russia which President Vladimir Putin has framed as a barometer of support for Russia's war in Ukraine. It is the first parliamentary election since Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022

key_facts.fact: Most anti-war candidates were excluded after the Supreme Court ruled the liberal Yabloko party, which wants a ceasefire, had breached electoral rules.
key_facts.excerpt: Most anti-war candidates have been excluded from the ballot after the Supreme Court ruled that the liberal Yabloko party - which wants a ceasefire - had breached electoral rules

key_facts.fact: More than 350 Ukrainian drones targeted Moscow on Friday morning; Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said most were destroyed on an outer perimeter and 64 were shot down as they approached the city.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 350 Ukrainian drones targeted the Russian capital on Friday morning, Moscow's mayor reported... Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on social media that most of the 350 drones sent towards the capital overnight had been destroyed at an outer defensive perimeter, with 64 shot down as they approached the city.

key_facts.fact: Voting runs until 18:00 GMT on Sunday and Moscow has also organised balloting in occupied parts of Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Voting runs until 18:00 GMT on Sunday. Moscow has also organised balloting in occupied parts of Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defence Ministry said on Friday it struck a Nova Poshta logistics hub near Odesa and a cargo vessel in the port of Chornomorsk; a Russian drone attack injured five people, including three children, in the Kyiv region.
key_facts.excerpt: The Russian Defence Ministry said on Friday that its forces had struck a logistics hub belonging to Ukrainian postal company Nova Poshta near the Black Sea port city of Odesa, as well as a cargo vessel in the nearby port of Chornomorsk... A Russian drone attack on Friday morning injured five people, including three children, in the Kyiv region

key_facts.fact: US-brokered peace talks are stuck on territory: Zelenskyy said negotiators are discussing a Ukrainian withdrawal from Donetsk in exchange for Russian forces not entering it, plus a joint format for the occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. negotiators foresee Ukrainian forces withdrawing from the Donetsk region, with the compromise being that Russian forces do not enter that territory, Zelenskyy said... The Americans have suggested a joint format to manage the plant, and negotiators are discussing how that might work

sources.title: Voting begins in Russian parliamentary election which Putin has cast as barometer of support for war
Ukraine fires drone barrage as Russia launches elections
Zelenskyy says US-led peace talks wrestling with Russian demands for Ukrainian territory

stories.headline: US sanctions Iranian exchange BitBank, the bitcoin rail behind Hormuz transit tolls

key_facts.fact: On September 17 the Treasury's OFAC designated BitBank, an Iranian digital asset exchange controlled by sanctioned financier Babak Zanjani, plus its developer Pishtaz Simorgh and three Zanjani associates.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated BitBank, a priority digital assets venture controlled by OFAC-designated Iranian financier Babak Zanjani... Today's designations also include BitBank's developer, Pishtaz Simorgh Electronic Trade Company (Pishtaz Simorgh) and three associates of Zanjani

key_facts.fact: Treasury said Zanjani used BitBank between June and July to move hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
key_facts.excerpt: Between June and July of this year, Zanjani utilized BitBank to facilitate the transfer of hundreds of millions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin to the IRGC.

key_facts.fact: Since June, the sanctioned Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority — the body Tehran uses to sell ships safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz — has used BitBank to pass its collections to the regime.
key_facts.excerpt: Since June of this year, OFAC-designated Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority has used BitBank to transfer payments it received to the Iranian regime.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said efforts to finance Iran with cryptocurrency are "not beyond OFAC's reach."
key_facts.excerpt: "Today's designations of Iranian digital asset infrastructure make perfectly clear that efforts to finance the Iranian regime using cryptocurrencies are not beyond OFAC's reach," said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.

key_facts.fact: The action falls under "Operation Economic Outcast," launched by Bessent on August 24 as a continuation of the earlier "Economic Fury" campaign, under which OFAC hit Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex in June and Shelbit and Aban Tether in August.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest action falls under a continuation of Economic Fury called "Operation Economic Outcast," a broader campaign launched on Aug. 24... In June, OFAC sanctioned Nobitex, Iran's largest crypto exchange, along with Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex

key_facts.fact: The Hormuz bitcoin-settled maritime platform first surfaced in Iranian media in May, when Tehran said it targeted more than $10 billion in revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Hormuz Safe appears to be the formal entity behind a bitcoin-settled platform first reported by Iranian media in May... At the time, Iran said it was targeting more than $10 billion in revenue for the platform.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported the exchange was accused of processing payments for ships to transit safely through the Strait of Hormuz, part of Treasury's campaign to isolate Iran economically.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States announced sanctions on an Iranian cryptocurrency exchange controlled by sanctioned Iranian financier Babak Zanjani on Thursday, accusing it of processing payments for ships to transit safely through the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.title: Operation Economic Outcast Disrupts Digital Asset Exchange Enabling the Iranian Regime
US sanctions Iranian financier's crypto exchange, says it processes Hormuz payments

stories.headline: FDA approves Ultragenyx's Fayuvi, the first-ever treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome type A

key_facts.fact: On September 17 the FDA approved Fayuvi (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf), the first treatment for pediatric patients with MPS IIIA, or Sanfilippo syndrome type A, a fatal inherited disease that progressively destroys the brain and nervous system.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Fayuvi (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf), the first treatment for pediatric patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA), also known as Sanfilippo syndrome type A.

key_facts.fact: Until the approval there was no therapy designed to change the course of the disease; treatment was limited to managing symptoms.
key_facts.excerpt: Until today, treatment was limited to managing symptoms; there was no FDA-approved therapy designed to change the underlying course of the disease.

key_facts.fact: In the pivotal Transpher A trial, 17 treated patients scored 23.5 points higher on the Bayley-III cognitive scale than an untreated natural history cohort of 27 children (p<0.0001), with follow-up now extending nearly eight years.
key_facts.excerpt: FAYUVI-treated patients from the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (N=17) were compared to untreated patients with Sanfilippo syndrome Type A from an external, comparable natural history cohort (N=27). FAYUVI-treated patients (mITT) demonstrated a 23.5 point higher (p<0.0001) cognitive score over natural history

key_facts.fact: Fayuvi is Ultragenyx's second gene therapy and sixth FDA approval overall; the company received a Priority Review Voucher upon approval.
key_facts.excerpt: FAYUVI marks the second gene therapy approval, and sixth FDA approval overall, for Ultragenyx. The Company received a Priority Review Voucher upon FAYUVI approval

key_facts.fact: The one-time AAV9 gene therapy reached approval after a rocky path: the FDA issued a complete response letter in July 2025 and Ultragenyx resubmitted in January 2026 with longer-term neurologic and biomarker data.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval follows a complicated regulatory path: an earlier biologics license application for the therapy received a complete response letter from the FDA in July 2025, and the company resubmitted with additional longer-term neurologic and biomarker data in January 2026.

key_facts.fact: The therapy had orphan drug, fast track and breakthrough therapy designations.
key_facts.excerpt: Fayuvi was granted orphan drug and fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations. The FDA granted Fayuvi approval to Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical, Inc.

sources.title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Pediatric Patients with Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A
Ultragenyx Announces Approval of FAYUVI Gene Therapy, the First-Ever FDA-Approved Treatment for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A (MPS IIIA)
FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A

stories.headline: South Korea delays first project under its $350B US investment pact over loss-sharing terms

key_facts.fact: At a September 18 press conference, President Lee Jae-myung said parts of the working-level agreement on the $350 billion strategic investment in the US are hard to accept and are being renegotiated.
key_facts.excerpt: At a press conference held at the Blue House State Guest House on the 18th, when asked about the progress of negotiations on investments in the U.S., President Lee said, "The working-level negotiation team says an agreement has almost been reached, but after reviewing the details, there are parts I find difficult to agree with, so we are discussing them again."

key_facts.fact: The sticking points are recovery of invested capital, profit distribution and who absorbs losses, plus the structure of the umbrella investment vehicle (I-SPV).
key_facts.excerpt: Last-minute Disagreements Between South Korea and the U.S. Over Capital Recovery, Profit Distribution, and Loss Allocation... it appears that a final agreement has not been reached not only on investment projects that cannot ensure profitability but also on the operational structure of the umbrella-type Investment Special Purpose Vehicle (I-SPV)

key_facts.fact: Seoul postponed the planned announcement of its first investment project; the report to the National Assembly slipped from September 17 to September 22.
key_facts.excerpt: the National Assembly report—originally scheduled for the 17th—was postponed to the 22nd and the government's announcement was also put on hold

key_facts.fact: Lee stressed the sum at stake is roughly 500 trillion won of taxpayers' money and that Seoul secured the phrase "commercial rationality" in the MOU, language he said is absent from other countries' deals.
key_facts.excerpt: "We are talking about $350 billion—approximately 500 trillion won—which amounts to taxpayers' money."... "No compromise had been reached by 7:30 a.m. on the day of the second summit, but fortunately, we were able to include the phrase 'commercial rationality' as we had wanted," adding, "It is a phrase not found in agreements with other countries."

key_facts.fact: Separately, Washington has asked Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix to expand memory production facilities in the US with their own capital, outside the government fund.
key_facts.excerpt: It is reported that the U.S. government has requested that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix expand their memory semiconductor production facilities in the United States. This is a direct investment matter requiring individual companies to invest their own funds, rather than a project funded by the government-established fund

sources.title: Announcement of Investment in the U.S. Postponed at the Last Minute… Lee: "We Will Reach a Conclusion on Semiconductor Investment That Protects National Interests"

stories.headline: Milei sends Congress a Falklands bill punishing resource extraction, with a terror registry attached

key_facts.fact: Argentina's government sent Congress a National Sovereignty Defense Bill on Thursday, September 17, which Milei presented as "a milestone in the process of recovering" the Falklands.
key_facts.excerpt: Argentina's government sent Congress a National Sovereignty Defense Bill on Thursday, presented by President Javier Milei as "a milestone in the process of recovering" the Falklands

key_facts.fact: The bill replaces the 2011 Law 26,659 and extends penalties from hydrocarbons to any natural resource on the Argentine continental shelf; barred companies could lose the right to operate anywhere in Argentina.
key_facts.excerpt: replaces Law 26,659, in force since 2011, and broadens its scope: no longer just hydrocarbons, but any natural resource, renewable or not, on the Argentine continental shelf... Companies that are barred would risk being unable to operate anywhere in the country

key_facts.fact: It creates a National Security Council chaired by Milei that can order urgent measures — restricting FX and financial operations, freezing assets, suspending contracts and restricting foreign trade — and lets the armed forces protect strategic facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: The bill creates a National Security Council, chaired by Milei, empowered to order "urgent measures" in the face of a grave and imminent threat: restricting foreign exchange and financial operations, temporarily freezing funds and assets, suspending authorizations or contracts, and restricting foreign trade.

key_facts.fact: Its most contested element is a public registry of people linked to terrorism (RePET), run by the Financial Information Unit, where inclusion requires only "reasonable grounds for suspicion" and no prior criminal case, triggering immediate asset freezes.
key_facts.excerpt: Inclusion in the registry "will not be conditioned on the existence of a criminal case": "reasonable grounds for suspicion" of a link to terrorism suffice, or a designation by the UN Security Council. The measure immediately triggers the freezing of funds and assets

key_facts.fact: Hours before the bill reached Congress, a federal judge in Tierra del Fuego ordered Rockhopper Exploration and Navitas Petroleum to halt work on the 23-well Sea Lion project on environmental grounds.
key_facts.excerpt: federal judge Mariel Borruto, of Río Grande, Tierra del Fuego, had granted an injunction... The judge ordered Rockhopper Exploration and Navitas Petroleum Development and Production to refrain from starting or continuing work on the Sea Lion project, which envisions 23 wells

key_facts.fact: Milei said the Falklands strategy had been in the works for three years and was triggered by Trump's remark about reviewing US neutrality in the dispute, rejecting claims it is electioneering before the 2027 vote.
key_facts.excerpt: "Political analysts say we pushed Malvinas for image reasons and political opportunism. That's a massive stupidity," he said, adding that the strategy had been in the works for three years and that the trigger was a remark by US President Donald Trump about reviewing his country's neutral stance in the dispute.

sources.title: Milei sends Congress his Falklands sovereignty bill, with an anti-terrorism registry attached
